Holiday Booking Rush: How Hair Salons Fill the Calendar Through December

Nov 16, 2026The SocialDM Insights Team9 min read
Key takeaways
  • December books up in November: agree on extra hours with each stylist and text regulars two specific times before posting publicly.
  • Set Google special hours now for November 26, December 24, 25, 31 and January 1, and keep a waitlist owned by one person each day.
  • Rebook January at checkout with a specific date, starting the week of November 30.
  • Post same day openings on Instagram stories every morning and a weekly Google post with a booking button.

December books up in November. A guest who wants a gloss before her office party, a fresh cut before family photos or a blowout for New Year's Eve is picking her time right now. If your book does not show open spots she can grab in a few taps, she books the salon that does.

This is a week by week plan from Monday, November 16 to Thursday, December 31, 2026, plus a January plan so the quiet weeks after the holidays are already half full. Every step works with the tools a salon or independent stylist already has.

Why plan the holidays week by week?

Because the season is short and the dates are fixed. The National Retail Federation forecasts that 2026 holiday retail sales will grow 4.2% to $1.013 trillion over November 1 through December 31. That is retail, not salons, but it shows how much of your guests' time and money these two months claim. When people are busy, the salon that makes booking easiest has the edge.

Here are the dates that shape your book this year:

DateDayWhat it means for your book
November 26ThursdayThanksgiving. Most guests want their appointment Tuesday or Wednesday before.
November 27FridayBlack Friday. A natural day to open gift cards.
November 28SaturdaySmall Business Saturday. Local shoppers are looking for independent businesses.
December 24ThursdayChristmas Eve. A short day for most salons, and a busy morning.
December 25FridayChristmas Day. Closed for most.
December 31ThursdayNew Year's Eve. Blowouts and updos, then an early close.
January 1, 2027FridayNew Year's Day, then a long weekend before January really starts.

Week of November 16: How do you open the book without burning out the team?

Decide your extra hours now, before guests ask. Agree with each stylist on exactly which extra shifts they will work. Patterns that work well:

  • Add one early morning or one late evening per stylist per week, not both. Tired stylists make mistakes on color.
  • Open a Sunday or Monday in December if you are normally closed, for the busiest two weeks only (December 13 and 14, December 20 and 21).
  • Protect long services. Block a few color and extension slots early in the season, and keep the last two weeks for faster services: blowouts, glosses, trims, bang trims and updos.
  • Put every extra hour into your booking system now, so guests see real availability instead of a full calendar.

Then tell your regulars first. Send a short text or email before you post anything publicly:

"Hi Jess, our December book opens to regulars today before we post it anywhere. Want me to save your usual color? Friday the 18th at 10 and Tuesday the 22nd at 2 are still open. Here is the link to grab one."

Two specific times are easier to answer than "let me know when works." They turn a maybe into a yes or no.

Also this week, set your Google holiday hours. Google's special hours guide walks through it: open your Business Profile, choose Edit profile, then Hours, and add each date under Special hours. Google suggests upcoming holidays and recommends confirming them even if your hours do not change. Set Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year's Eve and New Year's Day, plus any extra Sunday or Monday you are opening. One detail people miss: special hours only show if your regular hours are set to "Open with main hours."

Also the week of November 16: How do you set up a waitlist that actually fills gaps?

Build the list before you need it. A cancellation on December 19 is only worth something if you can fill it within the hour.

  1. Turn on your booking system's waitlist if it has one, or start a simple shared list with name, phone, service, stylist and the days they can come in.
  2. Ask for the list on every full day. When a guest cannot get the time she wants, the answer is "Can I put you on the list for Thursday? If something opens, you get a text first."
  3. Decide who sends the text. One person owns the waitlist each day. When a slot opens, they text the first three matches at once and give it to the first reply.
  4. Remind guests of your cancellation policy in every confirmation. Keep it friendly and clear: how much notice you need and what happens if they miss it.

A waitlist text can be this short: "A 3:30 blowout just opened today with Maya. Reply YES and it is yours."

This is also the week to make your public announcement. Post on Instagram and add a Google post. Google lets you schedule posts and set them to repeat, and update and event posts can include a button that links to your booking page. A simple update works: "December appointments are open. Extra evening hours added on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Book online."

Week of November 23: What should you do Thanksgiving week?

Expect Tuesday, November 24 and Wednesday, November 25 to be packed, then a quiet Thursday and a different kind of weekend.

  • Thanksgiving, November 26: closed for most. Make sure Google says so.
  • Black Friday, November 27: open gift card sales online if you have not already. Keep it brief: one post, one email, one sign at the front desk.
  • Small Business Saturday, November 28: a good day for a story that shows your team and your space, with a reminder that you are local and independent.

Gift cards deserve a short note. The NRF reported in December 2025 that 43% of holiday shoppers planned to buy at least one gift card last season, with total gift card spending expected to reach $29 billion. Under federal rules summarized by the FTC, money on a gift card generally cannot expire for at least five years from purchase, and inactivity fees are limited. Many states add their own rules, so check with your attorney or accountant before you print terms, and do not put an expiration date on a card without that advice.

Week of November 30: When should you rebook January?

Start now, at checkout, with every guest. January feels far away in the chair, which is exactly why it works. A guest who leaves with a date in the book has a reason to return. A guest who leaves with "I'll call you" often drifts.

Give every stylist the same one line script:

"Your color will be ready for a refresh around the third week of January. Want me to save Tuesday the 19th at 11 before the book fills up after the holidays?"

Two tips make this stick. First, the stylist offers a specific date based on the service, not a vague "January." Second, the front desk does not let a guest leave without being asked. Track a simple number each day: how many guests left with a next visit booked. Share it at the morning huddle.

Week of December 7: How do you post last minute openings on Google and Instagram?

Post openings the morning they appear, in plain words, with one way to book. Guests scrolling at 8am want to know if they can get in today.

WhereWhat to postWhen
Instagram stories"Today: 11:00 trim with Ana, 4:30 blowout with Maya." Add a link sticker to your booking page.Every morning by 8, again at noon if spots remain
Instagram close friends listThe same openings, first, to your regularsBefore the public story
Google post"Limited openings this week. Evening times added Tuesday and Thursday. Book online."Weekly, with a booking button
Text to waitlistThe specific time and stylistThe moment a slot opens

Keep the Google post about the week, not the hour. Stories and texts handle same day openings. If your Google profile, website and booking page still show old hours or a broken link, fix that first. Our guide to getting more salon bookings from Google Maps covers the profile basics.

Weeks of December 14 and December 21: How do you keep the peak running smoothly?

Small leaks cost the most in this stretch:

  • Confirm every appointment two days ahead and the morning of. Ask guests to reply if plans change, so you can text the waitlist.
  • Run a five minute morning huddle. Open slots, waitlist matches, who is posting the story, and how many January rebooks yesterday.
  • Keep a short service menu for the final days. Blowouts, glosses, trims and updos move the line. Save big color changes for guests already in the book.
  • Christmas Eve, Thursday, December 24: open early, close early, and post your hours on stories the day before.

December 26 to 31: What should you do the week after Christmas?

Turn your attention to January while the book is still busy. Gift card recipients start looking for a time right away, and New Year's Eve, Thursday, December 31, brings a last wave of blowouts and updos.

  • Post a "used a gift card? here is how to book" story with simple steps.
  • Text guests you saw in early November who have not rebooked.
  • Confirm Google shows your New Year's Eve and New Year's Day hours.
  • Write down what worked: which extra hours filled, which did not, how many waitlist fills, how many January rebooks. That note is your 2027 plan.

What should a salon's January plan look like?

January starts Friday, January 1, 2027, so the first real week begins Monday, January 4. Plan it now so you are not starting from an empty book.

WeekFocus
January 4Confirm everyone who rebooked in December. Welcome gift card guests with a warm first visit and ask them to rebook before they leave.
January 11Text guests from October and early November who are now due. Offer two specific times.
January 18Post education content: winter hair care, how long a gloss lasts, what a trim schedule looks like. Ask happy guests for a Google review.
January 25Open the Valentine's book. February 14, 2027 falls on a Sunday, so Friday the 12th and Saturday the 13th will go first.

January is also a good time to train the team on checkout rebooking while the pace is calmer.

Your holiday checklist for this week

  • Agree on extra hours with every stylist and load them into your booking system.
  • Text regulars with two specific December times before posting publicly.
  • Start a waitlist and choose one person to own it each day.
  • Give stylists the January rebooking line.
  • Set up gift cards and check your state's gift card rules.

Questions we hear

When should a hair salon start holiday marketing?

Now. Guests plan December appointments in November, so open your extra hours, message regulars first and set Google holiday hours in the week of November 16.

How do I set holiday hours on Google for my salon?

In your Business Profile, choose Edit profile, then Hours, then add each date under Special hours. Google may suggest upcoming holidays for you to review. Your regular hours must be set to Open with main hours for special hours to show.

How do I fill last minute cancellations in December?

Keep a waitlist with each guest's service, stylist and available days. When a slot opens, one person texts the first few matches with the exact time and gives it to the first reply. Post same day openings on Instagram stories each morning.

Can salon gift cards have an expiration date?

Federal rules summarized by the FTC say money on a gift card generally cannot expire for at least five years from purchase, and many states have stricter rules. Check with your attorney or accountant before setting any terms.
